## Summary

Shinwa Industries (China) Ltd. is an electronics manufacturer in Huizhou, Guangdong, established in July 1986 as a China, Japan and Hong Kong joint venture with US$19.5 million registered capital [3]. Its group site describes Shinwa as a JVCKENWOOD company, and lists the Huizhou Pingnan site for EMS services, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi modules and battery management systems, and a Dongjiang site for EMS, optical pick-ups and factory automation [2]. The IEEE registry lists two MA-L blocks under two capitalisations of this name, both at Huizhou addresses [1].

A MAC in a Shinwa block is most likely a radio module inside another company's product, above all in-car equipment: the company lists car CD/DVD cores and servo decoders, car GPS/Bluetooth modules and DAB, CMMB and ISDB-T broadcast modules, and names Hitachi, Philips, Siemens VDO, Delphi, Sony, Visteon, Kenwood, NEC, LG and Huawei among its long-term customers [3]. So the brand on the device is likely a car head unit or audio maker rather than Shinwa. The radio list is inferred from the module types the company names; no Wi-Fi generation or Bluetooth version is documented in the sources consulted [2][3].

The profile page carries no date, so its customer list may be historical [3]. Silicon, FCC grantee codes and security history are not listed: fccid.io and fcc.report refused requests from the session that wrote this entry, no teardown was found, and nothing is filled in from memory. The registry also has a separate SHINWA INDUSTRIES, INC. in Tokyo, holding an MA-S block, which this entry does not cover [4].
